l@/$u?e!wH[rh`RxEX@s.text:
--Want to mod the game?--
1. CUSTOM CHARACTERS:

(Adding the character)
- In the "Opponent" sprite, make the following, replacing Char with your character's name:
1. 4 costumes: CharIdle1, CharIdle2, CharIdle3 and CharIdle4. Unless you want to customize the idle animation, the first costume is the static idle sprite and the other 3 are for the head bop animation that plays to the beat of the song.
2. CharLeft1 and CharLeft2
3. CharUp1 and CharUp2
4. CharDown1 and CharDown2
5. CharRight1 and CharRight2

(Adding the health bar icon)
- In the "Health Bar" sprite, make a new costume with your character's name and design it however you'd like
- If you want the character to have a different icon when their health is low, add another costume called CharDanger but replacing Char with your character's name

(Testing your character)
-Go into any song, press 7 and click change character, then enter your character's name. Then press 7 again to restart the song

(Fixing offsets)
-If your character is in the wrong place, find the "Fix offsets " define block and change the "if charname == MyChar" replacing MyChar with your character's name and change the x and y variables and size in there

2. CUSTOM SONGS:

(Adding the song)
-Add your song's instrumental into sounds in backdrop (Name must be SongName_Inst replacing SongName with your song's name.
-Add your song's vocals into sounds in SongVoices (Name must be SongName_Voices replacing SongName with your song's name.) This is optional if your song doesnt have voices.

(Adding to freeplay)
-In the "Menu" sprite, make 2 new costumes, one called SongName-1 and another called SongName-2 (Replace SongName with your song's name). These sprites will be used in the freeplay menu, -1 for not selected, -2 for selected.
-Add your song's name to the "Levels" list.

(Charting the song)
-Open your song from freeplay and press 7 to open the debug menu.
-You can do one of 3 things:

1. Click "Load song from json" and copy the contents of an fnf json chart file into the text box
2. Press "Clear markers" then play through your song with ghost tapping on and press keys in time with the voices to add the key presses to the markers list. Then return to the debug menu and add those notes manually or press auto add marker to have them automatically added to the chart.
3. Manually add the notes using the "New note" button

-Once you're done, right click on the top of the "Chart" list and click export. This will download a txt file.
-Make a new list (You might want to use your song's name to avoid confusion) and right click the top of it and select "Import"
-Choose the txt file that has just downloaded.
(If you make changes to the chart, you will have this export and import method again)

(Making the song load correctly)
-Right click the code labelled "Freeplay song loader" to the right of this comment and press duplicate.
-Replace "MySong" with your song's name.
-Change both instances of the "_Sprite" list to the list where you imported your chart.
-Add it onto the end of the "Replace chart" block (Scroll right)

-Right click the code labelled "Custom song data" to the right of this comment and press duplicate.
-Replace "MySong" with your song's name.
-Change the set song tempo to be set to your song's bpm (Optional, but recommended)
-Change the set P2 to be set to the character you want the song to use's name.
(-Change the set scroll speed to be set to your song's default scroll speed.
-Change the set arrow offset to be set to your song's default arrow offset) these are both optional
-Change the set bg to be set to your song's background.
-Add it near the end of the song selected block before "Replace chart (Song)"

(Adding custom song properties)
-Scroll to where you change the song tempo, p2 etc and find your song's if statement.
-Open the __CUTOM SONG PROPERTIES LIST and read through the properties.
-If you find a property you want to add, place a "add (PROPERTYNAME) to CurSongInfo" (Replacing PROPERTYNAME with the property's name) inside your song's if statement along with the other variable setters. If it has - Value 1:, - Value 2 etc after it, the property has extra settings which you will have to add as well right after the property name.
By the way, you might want to look at the other songs like elephant, deleted and bitmap for examples of this if it confuses you

3. CUSTOM WEEKS:
-In the "Menu" sprite, make 2 new costumes, one called --Week(num)-1, the other called --Week(num)-2 (Replace (num) with the number which is one above the current last week)
-Add your song names to the "Weeks" list and then add --(num)-- replacing (num) with your week's number

4. CUSTOM NOTE TYPES:
-In the "Notes" sprite, add your custom arrow's costume (Use the default note as a template)
-Under the "Get custom properties ()" define block, add an if statement checking if the type value from the define block is equal to your custom note's name
-Like adding custom song properties, Open the __CUTOM NOTE PROPERTIES LIST and read through the properties.
-If you find a property you want to add, place a "add (PROPERTYNAME) to Note custom properties" (Replacing PROPERTYNAME with the property's name) inside your note's if statement. If it has - Value 1:, - Value 2 etc after it, the property has extra settings which you will have to add as well right after the property name.
(Making your note always stay when exporting but deleting custom notes)
-This should only be done with notes that must be hit
-Add your note's name to the __KEEP NOTES DURING EXPORT list
(Making your notes change in easy mode)
Find the "define Fix easy mode note types" block and add an if statement checking if notetype is equal to your note's name
If you want the note to become a default note, use a "Set notetype to ()"
If you want the note to disappear, use a "Set notetype to (-del)"

5. ADDING DIALOG
-In the "Dialogue" sprite, add a new if statement checking if the song variable is equal to your song's name under the run dialog broadcast (Must be before the "Clear dialogue" broadcast is sent)
-Use the Dialog () () () () custom block inside your if statement to add lines of dialog. The first value is the text, the second value is how long of a break is in between each letter, the third value is the portrait that the dialog line uses
-You can add your own dialogue portraits for characters in the dialogue sprite's costumes.
-The fourth value of the custom block is for dialog effects.open the __CUSTOM DIALOG EFFECTS LIST and pick any that you like the look of. Then you can put them in the box of the custom block, seperating each with a comma and using a colon to seperate it from the values
(EXAMPLE: Instant,Shout:3,Spinny)

6. CUSTOMIZING MAIN MENU
-Open the ___Main menu options list and add, remove and move the options as you please.
-At the moment, you can only use Storymode, Freeplay, Options and Credits in this list
